events.title: Birth of Augustus, Rome's First Emperor
events.description: Gaius Octavius, later known as Augustus, was born on this day in 63 BCE. He rose from the turmoil that followed Julius Caesar's assassination to become the first Roman emperor.
events.significance: Augustus ended decades of civil war and set up the imperial system. He began the Pax Romana, a long period of relative peace and stability across the Mediterranean world.

events.title: Capture of John André Exposes Benedict Arnold
events.description: Patriot militiamen captured British Major John André near Tarrytown, New York. They found papers on him showing that American General Benedict Arnold planned to hand over West Point.
events.significance: The discovery foiled one of the most dangerous betrayals of the American Revolution. It also made Arnold's name a lasting byword for treason.

events.title: Neptune Is Observed for the First Time
events.description: Johann Gottfried Galle of the Berlin Observatory found Neptune. He used the mathematical predictions of French astronomer Urbain Le Verrier to point his telescope at the right spot.
events.significance: Neptune was the first planet located by calculation before it was seen. The discovery was seen as a triumph for Newtonian physics.

events.title: Death of Sigmund Freud
events.description: Sigmund Freud, the Austrian neurologist who founded psychoanalysis, died in London at age 83. He had fled Nazi-occupied Austria the year before.
events.significance: Freud's ideas about the unconscious mind, dreams and early experience changed psychology, medicine, literature and popular culture.

events.title: Birth of Bruce Springsteen
events.description: Bruce Springsteen was born in Long Branch, New Jersey. He became known as 'The Boss' for his storytelling songs and marathon live shows.
events.significance: Springsteen became one of rock music's most celebrated songwriters. His work chronicles working-class American life.
